events.detail: Wilson vetoed CB 121283, the RV permit program in Councilmember Strauss's Vehicle Resident Assistance Program, and signed the other four bills, including one that gives the city more authority to lease land for safe lots and RV storage. events.title: Council schedules vote on overriding the RV permit veto for Thursday, Nov. 12
events.detail: The Seattle City Council has scheduled a vote on Thursday, Nov. 12 on whether to override Mayor Wilson's veto of Council Bill 121283, the RV permit program. An override needs a two-thirds majority. Wilson signed the other four bills in the RV package, including one that expands the city's authority to open safe parking lots and storage sites. Councilmember Dan Strauss, the bill's sponsor, has said he will seek the override. Council members have until Dec. 2 to vote on an override.

events.title: Council fails to override mayor's RV permit veto
events.detail: The City Council voted 5-4 on Nov. 12 to override Mayor Wilson's veto of CB 121283, the RV permit bill. Six votes were needed, so the veto stands. Councilmember Rob Saka had voted for the bill in October and did not vote to override. The other four bills in the Vehicle Resident Assistance Program package were signed on Nov. 2 and remain in effect. They include CB 121279, which lets the Finance and Administrative Services director sign leases for safe lots, safe storage and other resources for vehicle residents. The mayor's Nov. 3 executive order stays in place. It directs outreach funding, the opening of two RV safe lots for 182 vehicle residents, and a working group with recommendations due in 60 days. The mayor's office says it will send any needed legislation to the council by March 31, 2027. Councilmember Strauss, the bill's sponsor, said the city is 'on track' to add two safe lots.
